plans.name: Positive prepaid credit balance
plans.note: PRO not mandatory: any user/org with positive balance may run Jobs. Subscription compute credits can also apply. Concurrency / parallel-job limits are not published (docs only say "Many Jobs can run in parallel"); default job timeout is 30 min, configurable.

plans.name: PRO (optional)
plans.note: Optional personal Hub subscription; Jobs do not require it. $2 monthly general compute credit applies to Jobs.

plans.name: Team (optional)
plans.note: Optional organization plan; $2 general compute credit per seat/month, automatically applied before PAYG.

plans.name: Enterprise (optional)
plans.note: From $50/user/month; $2 general compute credit per seat/month. Jobs remain PAYG.

plans.name: Enterprise Plus (optional)
plans.note: Custom price; $2/seat/month general compute credit plus additional compute credit equal to 5% of ACV.

caveats: Public Jobs rates, not Spaces free hardware. Harbor hf-sandbox wraps Jobs; an interactive wrapper does not change underlying job billing. Jobs bill Starting and Running, per minute; builds free. Exposed ports add $0.01/job-hour.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
Re-checked 2026-09-28: jobs-pricing and jobs-overview publish no concurrent-job cap, so plan.concurrency stays null (unknown, not unlimited).

fleet.verification: Positive compute credit balance required; subscription-included credits can be used.
fleet.notes: Jobs now available to any user/organization with positive balance, not only PRO. No new-account simultaneous job/GPU quota or fleet-scale approval SLA found. Do not substitute ZeroGPU Space daily minutes or Hub API rate limits.

snapshot_auto.quote: Ephemeral disk doesn't survive the Job, so write anything you want to keep to a [Storage Bucket](./storage-buckets) mounted read-write, or push it to the Hub as a dataset.
snapshot_auto.note: Jobs are run-to-completion containers; state is lost when the job ends. Persistence only via bucket volume mounts.

harness_api.quote: You can open an interactive SSH session into a running Job to debug, inspect, or work directly inside the container.
harness_api.note: Jobs API/CLI (hf jobs run/uv run/logs/ssh) is generic container execution; no first-party API to drive Claude Code/Codex etc. hf-sandbox on PyPI ('Modal-style sandbox API on top of Hugging Face Jobs') lists no author and is not documented by HF as first-party.

ingress_rules.quote: Each exposed port is reachable at `https://<job_id>--<port>.hf.jobs` and requires an HF token with `read` access to the job's namespace
ingress_rules.note: Ports are only exposed when chosen with --expose; public proxy URLs are token-authenticated. SSH opt-in (--ssh), restricted to users with Write access via registered SSH keys. Network groups give private job-to-job connectivity.

secret_proxy.quote: # Pass secrets - they will be encrypted server side
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are encrypted server-side but delivered to the job as environment variables (script reads os.environ["MY_SECRET"]). Bucket volume mounts are authorized with the user's HF identity at job creation so the script needs no token for them (jobs-manage), but that is not a general credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Mount Hugging Face repositories (models, datasets), [Storage Buckets](./storage-buckets), or local directories as volumes in your job container using `-v` or `--volume`.
volume_attach.note: Network (object-storage-backed, lazily fetched) mounts, not block volumes. Buckets read-write by default (:ro optional); model/dataset repos always read-only. Bucket storage billed per TB.

volume_shared.quote: Volume mounts in [Jobs](./jobs) and [Spaces](./spaces) are the same idea as `hf-mount`, managed for you by the platform — no extra setup needed. Buckets are mounted read-write by default.
volume_shared.note: Any number of jobs (and Spaces) can mount the same bucket (read-write) or dataset/model repo (read-only); concurrent multi-writer semantics are not documented explicitly. Scheduled jobs mount the same synced folder on every trigger.

isolation.quote: Docker Jobs Specify the Docker image and the command to run as you would with docker: >>> hf jobs run ubuntu echo "Hello from t..."
isolation.note: Jobs run as Docker containers (UV or arbitrary Docker image) on shared multi-tenant hosts; no VM/microVM isolation documented.

docker_inside.quote: Docker Jobs Specify the Docker image and the command to run as you would with docker
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a Job itself is a single container; no privileged mode, docker socket, or docker-in-docker support is documented.

nested_virt.quote: Jobs run in isolated compute environments billed per minute while Starting or Running.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — container isolation with no /dev/kvm or nested virtualization documented.

desktop.quote: Run any workload ... Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Jobs is a batch/CLI container-execution product, no GUI desktop offered.

browser.quote: Run any workload ... Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no managed/embedded browser product for Jobs.

computer_use.quote: Run any workload ... Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no screenshot/click desktop-driving API.

anti_bot.quote: Pricing and Billing ... Jobs bill Starting and Running, per minute
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Jobs is a generic compute-container product, not a browser/scraping product.

captcha_solving.quote: Pricing and Billing ... Jobs bill Starting and Running, per minute
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving feature for a generic compute job product.

egress_ip_type.quote: Each exposed port is reachable at https://<job_id>--<port>.hf.jobs and requires an HF token with read access to the job's namespace
egress_ip_type.note: No residential/mobile egress product documented; outbound traffic runs from HF's own datacenter infrastructure.

ssh.quote: You can open an interactive SSH session into a running Job to debug, inspect, or work directly inside the container.

snapshot.quote: Ephemeral disk doesn't survive the Job, so write anything you want to keep to a Storage Bucket mounted read-write, or push it to the Hub as a dataset.
snapshot.note: Jobs are run-to-completion containers with no filesystem or memory snapshot/checkpoint capability; persistence only via mounted bucket/dataset volumes.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Ephemeral disk doesn't survive the Job, so write anything you want to keep to a Storage Bucket mounted read-write, or push it to the Hub as a dataset.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI to take an on-demand snapshot/checkpoint of a Job is documented.

fork.quote: Run any workload ... Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Jobs starts a fresh container from an image/script; no clone-a-running-machine feature documented.

fork_running.quote: Run any workload ... Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no forking feature at all is documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Run any workload ... Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no fork/snapshot capability of any kind is documented.

pause_resume.quote: Jobs have a default timeout (30 minutes), after which they will automatically stop.
pause_resume.note: Jobs run to completion or are stopped by timeout/cancel; no pause-and-later-resume of a Job is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Run any workload ... Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Jobs are explicitly started (or scheduled), not woken by an inbound request to a sleeping instance.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Jobs have a default timeout (30 minutes), after which they will automatically stop.
auto_stop_idle.note: Stopping is a fixed/custom wall-clock timeout, not idle-usage detection; no idle-based auto-stop is documented.

live_resize.quote: Choose hardware for your workload ... flavor argument
live_resize.note: Hardware flavor is fixed at job creation via --flavor; no documented way to change CPU/RAM of a running Job without recreating it.

agent_harnesses.quote: Run any workload ... Python scripts ... Docker images
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Jobs offers generic Python/Docker execution; no preinstalled coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) templates documented for Jobs.

own_agent_api.quote: The Hugging Face MCP Server provides seamless access to Hugging Face's vast ecosystem of Models, Datasets, Research Papers and state-of-the-art AI tools.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — this is a discovery/search MCP server for the Hub, not a first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent API for Jobs.

mcp_server.quote: The Hugging Face MCP Server provides seamless access to Hugging Face's vast ecosystem of Models, Datasets, Research Papers and state-of-the-art AI tools.
mcp_server.note: HF ships an MCP server, but it exposes Hub search/discovery tools, not control of Jobs sandboxes (start/stop/manage a Job).

lang_python.quote: Use hf jobs uv run to run a Python script remotely. Specify its dependencies using --with or in a script header.

lang_node.quote: Use hf jobs run with a Docker image and the command to run. The image provides the tools and libraries your workload needs, whether you're using Python or another language.
lang_node.note: Node.js is not a first-party out-of-the-box runtime (only Python/UV is native); Node can only be reached by supplying your own Docker image.

public_ipv4.quote: Each exposed port is reachable at https://<job_id>--<port>.hf.jobs and requires an HF token with read access to the job's namespace
public_ipv4.note: Exposed ports are reached through HF's proxy hostname (hf.jobs), not a per-machine public IPv4 address.

egress_allowlist.quote: Network Security ... Define your organization IP Ranges ... to enforce authenticated access to Hugging Face from your corporate network.
egress_allowlist.note: The only documented "network security" control is inbound IP-range login enforcement for the Hub; no outbound/egress allowlist or no-internet mode for Jobs is documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: Network Security ... Define your organization IP Ranges ... to enforce authenticated access to Hugging Face from your corporate network.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress rules for Jobs are documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Docker Jobs Specify the Docker image and the command to run as you would with docker
guest_firewall.note: derived: Jobs is container isolation (not a full VM/microVM), so guest-side nftables/iptables control is not assumed available.

static_egress_ip.quote: Pricing and Billing ... Jobs bill Starting and Running, per minute
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed/dedicated outbound IP for Jobs is documented.

windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — all published Jobs flavors are Linux containers; no Windows machine option.

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Jobs runs Linux Docker containers only, no macOS hardware option.

arm64.note: not offered: no ARM CPU flavor is listed among the published CPU/GPU flavors.

self_host.quote: Pricing and Billing ... Jobs bill Starting and Running, per minute
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Jobs is a hosted PAYG service on huggingface.co; no self-hosted Jobs runtime is offered.

byoc.quote: Pricing and Billing ... Jobs bill Starting and Running, per minute
byoc.note: not offered: no deploy-into-your-own-cloud-account option for Jobs is documented.

open_source.quote: This server is Open Source, click the link below for details of alternative deployment options
open_source.note: The huggingface_hub client and the MCP server are open source, but the Jobs execution backend/service itself is closed-source hosted infrastructure.

sso.quote: Single Sign-On (SAML & OIDC) Connect securely with your identity provider
sso.note: Org-level Enterprise feature covering the Hub account (which gates Jobs access), not a Jobs-specific SSO.

eu_data_residency.quote: Storage Regions Choose where your repository data lives ... US or EU
eu_data_residency.note: Regions apply to repository/storage data location (Enterprise/Enterprise Plus); no confirmation that Jobs compute execution itself is pinned to the EU region.

soc2.quote: Hugging Face is also SOC2 Type 2 certified, meaning we provide security certification to our customers and actively monitor and patch any security weaknesses.
soc2.note: Company-wide certification covering the Hub platform (Jobs runs on Hub infrastructure).

hipaa.quote: Hugging Face can also offer Business Associate Addendums or GDPR data processing agreements through an Enterprise Plan.
hipaa.note: BAA available, but only through an Enterprise Plan contract, not by default on PAYG Jobs usage.

persistent_disk.quote: Ephemeral disk doesn’t survive the Job, so write anything you want to keep to a Storage Bucket mounted read-write, or push it to the Hub as a dataset.
persistent_disk.note: Not a real contradiction: HF Jobs are run-to-completion containers with no pause/resume or automatic-snapshot feature at all (jobs-overview, jobs-pricing, and jobs-configuration contain zero mentions of pause, resume, or snapshot). The 'volumes' present are network-mounted external Storage Buckets / HF repos attached at job creation (volume_attach/volume_shared), not a persistent disk for the job's own filesystem — the job's local/ephemeral disk is explicitly documented as not surviving the job. So there is no first-party mechanism that keeps the job's own filesystem across a stop/pause; persistent_disk=false is confirmed, and volumes/snapshot_auto/pause_resume being null/false in the card is consistent, not contradictory.

max_session_h.quote: Jobs have a default timeout (30 minutes), after which they will automatically stop. ... You can specify a custom timeout value using the --timeout parameter when running a job. ... -- timeout 1d # 1 day
max_session_h.note: Only a default (30 min) is published; the timeout is fully user-configurable to arbitrary values (docs show examples up to '1d' and note larger values like 7200s/2h are fine) with no documented maximum cap found on jobs-configuration, jobs-pricing, or jobs-overview, so treated as effectively unbounded ("none") rather than a hard provider-imposed ceiling.
